tagline: North from Boone along a river new in name only.
intro: NC 194 leaves Boone northbound on what was once called the Old Buffalo Trail, narrow and curving through the state's thickest Christmas tree country to Todd and on to Baldwin, where the byway pauses. US 221 carries on through West Jefferson and Jefferson, and the byway takes up again on NC 88 for the last ten miles to Laurel Springs.
This is the valley of the New, which despite its name is counted by some geologists among the oldest rivers in the world. It flows north, cutting through the ridges on its long way round to the Ohio.

moments.title: Todd
moments.text: The railroad they called the Virginia Creeper, for its slow climb up the grades, came for Todd's timber, and when the timber played out in 1934 the train went too.

moments.title: West Jefferson
moments.text: A town the railroad made, incorporated in 1909, that at one time had the only cheese factory in the southeastern United States.

moments.title: Laurel Springs
moments.text: The end of the road, named for a spring that runs out of laurel-covered rocks, sits where NC 88 meets NC 18 and the Blue Ridge Parkway passes straight through.

practical: The route is not recommended for recreational vehicles or buses.
